findings.title: FileResponder re-stat after open leaks the just-opened stream when the file vanished
findings.description: The P5-001 fix calls ((FileResourceResolver) r).stat(path) after r.open(path) outside any try. FileResourceResolver.stat -> file() -> check() throws FileNotFoundException when the file was removed or became unreachable (rm + cp deploys, symlink flip). The exception leaves respond() with 'in' open and never closed (only the later answer() try closes it), so each such request leaks a descriptor until GC finalization; under a deploy that deletes a hot asset repeatedly this can exhaust fds. The second-pass failure also surfaces as a plain IOException('file changed while it was answered') which the caller presumably maps to 500 instead of the 404/503 a missing file gets.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the re-stat in try { ... } catch (IOException | RuntimeException e) { in.close(); throw e; } (or compute the comparison inside a try/finally that closes on every non-handoff path); map the changed-twice case to FileNotFoundException/503.

findings.title: Pool.completeAll starts one new thread per open stream, unbounded and with an uncaught Error path
findings.description: The P7-002 fix replaces the sequential abort with 'new Thread(...).start()' per stream. With maxSseStreams up to its configured limit (hundreds/thousands) shutdown creates that many threads at once, right when the container is closing; a Thread.start() OutOfMemoryError (an Error, not caught) leaves the loop midway: streams after the failing one are never aborted/removed and the exception escapes ServletAdapter.stop before p.shutdownNow(). The join loop also adds up: each stuck thread (a container call that does not return, not just the 250 ms lock wait) costs ABORT_WAIT_MILLIS*4 = 1 s sequentially, so N stuck aborts overshoot stop by N seconds, contradicting the 'waits must not add up' comment. Threads are daemon so no permanent leak, but they are unnamed-per-stream duplicates of the pool.
findings.suggested_fix: Do the aborts on the existing SSE pool or a small fixed executor (or set aborted=true on all, then complete on one helper thread), join against one shared deadline (not per thread), and catch Throwable around start so the remaining streams are still handled in the calling thread.

findings.title: Shutdown still skips adapter.release() and loses the Error when the logger flush/close throws an Error
findings.description: P2-002 was fixed for adapter stop/release and owned close, but SafeLogger.flushAndClose catches only Exception. In runShutdownSequence the call at DefaultRestApp.java:736 sits between the owned-close step and a.release(): an Error from logger.flush()/close() (e.g. NoClassDefFoundError in a torn-down webapp, or an AssertionError from a test logger) exits the try body, so a.release() never runs (TinyHttpd threads are not awaited, Servlet SSE pool is not shut down) and the Error is not routed through firstError/log. TERMINATED is still reached via finally, so impact is limited to the release step.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch Throwable in the shutdown sequence around SafeLogger.flushAndClose (record via firstError) or make flushAndClose itself return the first Error; keep a.release() after it.

findings.title: NaruServe-kotlin languageVersion/apiVersion 1.9 does not make the module consumable from Kotlin 1.9/2.0: the api dependency still pins kotlin-stdlib 2.2.0
findings.description: The fix sets languageVersion/apiVersion KOTLIN_1_9 so the module's own metadata is 1.9, but the same build declares ':NaruServe-kotlin' api -> org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib:2.2.0 (build.gradle:69, published as an api/compile dependency). A consumer on Kotlin 1.9.x or 2.0.x resolves the highest stdlib (2.2.0), whose class metadata (2.2) is newer than those compilers accept (current+1), so the original 'incompatible version of Kotlin' error class is not removed. The comment 'keeps Android apps on Kotlin 1.9/2.0 compiling' is therefore unverified; there is no test pinning the metadata level (e.g. a check of kotlin.Metadata mv in the produced classes) and docs/api/kotlin.md states no minimum Kotlin version.
findings.suggested_fix: Either also declare the stdlib dependency at the 1.9 level (kotlin-stdlib:1.9.x as api, consumers then upgrade it themselves) or state the real minimum Kotlin version in docs/api/kotlin.md; add a build check that reads the kotlin.Metadata mv of NaruServe-kotlin classes.

findings.title: Servlet adapter now throws IOException('exchange aborted') for every aborted non-SSE exchange, including routine client disconnects
findings.description: P7-001 is resolved (the connection no longer gets the terminating chunk), but the mechanism is a plain IOException without cause thrown out of service(). The core calls ex.abort() on any failed write, i.e. for a client that closes its socket during a download or an error render (Dispatcher.java:369, DefaultResponse.java:700/768). Jetty treats an EofException quietly but a bare IOException from a servlet is logged as a servlet failure (WARN/ERROR with stack trace) and, for an uncommitted response, triggers the container error dispatch/500 page; Tomcat logs it at ERROR. A flood of aborted downloads therefore floods the container log, which the previous silent behavior did not.
findings.suggested_fix: Throw only when it matters (response committed) and use a dedicated quiet exception or the container's own abort convention (rethrow the original IOException cause, or Jetty/Tomcat specific ClientAbort handling); at least document the log noise in docs/api/servlet.md.

findings.title: OwnedResources.closeAll drops every Error after the first without suppressing it
findings.description: The P2-001 fix keeps only the first Error; a second Error from another close() (catch (Error e) { firstError = firstError == null ? e : firstError; }) is discarded silently, while Exception failures are attached as suppressed. The diagnostic of a second broken resource is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: In the catch, call firstError.addSuppressed(e) when firstError != null.

findings.title: RotatingFileLogger writer can still die: closeStream() in the new Throwable catch handles IOException only
findings.description: The P8-001 fix catches Throwable from write() and calls closeStream(). closeStream catches only IOException, so an unchecked exception or Error from OutputStream.close() (the very state that follows an OutOfMemoryError or a broken stream) escapes drain() and kills the writer thread, i.e. the survive-an-Error guarantee does not hold for that path; the same hole existed in write()'s own catch.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch Throwable (except ThreadDeath) inside closeStream, or wrap the catch body in its own try/catch.

findings.title: flush() 5 s bound is a hard cut-off even for a writer that is only slow: shutdown can drop records the writer would have written
findings.description: flush() and close() each give up after waitMillis (5 s) whether the writer is stalled or merely draining a 1024-record backlog on slow storage; close() then abandonQueue() counts everything still queued as dropped even though the writer is running and would have written it. Up to 10 s (flush + close) can also be spent beyond the app's shutdown deadline because SafeLogger.flushAndClose does not take the deadline. Documented, but the progress of the writer is not considered (no reset of the deadline while the queue shrinks).
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the deadline while the queue length decreases (progress-based wait), or take the shutdown deadline into account.

findings.title: New tests are weaker than their names claim
findings.description: ServletAbortConnectionTest swallows the 10 s SocketTimeoutException (an IOException) as 'a reset', so a connection that is simply left hanging without a terminator also passes assertFalse(endsWith 0-chunk); it does not prove the connection ended abnormally. ServletStopSseTest.FR_SVL_006_AC3 asserts a 900..1600 ms wall-clock window (stop deadline 1 s + one 250 ms wait), 350 ms of slack on a loaded CI box. ReleaseScriptTextTest.fr_REL_002_AC5 only checks that two strings occur in release.gradle (a comment would satisfy it). SpoolPermissionsTest passes vacuously under umask 077 and on non-POSIX stores (assumeTrue).
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the read ended with -1/reset within a few seconds (not by timeout); widen or remove the upper timing bound and count aborted exchanges instead; assert the forwarded argument list of the child command; create the file with an explicit permissive umask-independent precondition.

unresolved.reason: module metadata is lowered to 1.9 but the api dependency kotlin-stdlib:2.2.0 still forces 2.2 metadata on consumers and nothing tests or documents the minimum (see R1-004).
